implementationDefaults.description: Deterministic thresholds and tie-breaks used by PracticeAI are engineering defaults, not prescriptions from the source document.
implementationDefaults.handInference: For a conventional two-staff piano part, staff 1 is treated as right hand and staff 2 as left hand; ambiguous cross-staff notation falls back to general analysis.

techniques.title: Octaves
detectionEvidence: Successive simultaneous pitch pairs exactly twelve semitones apart in one or both hands.
A scale-like octave run moves by no more than two semitones between neighboring attacks.
A progressive-groups exercise requires at least four consecutive octave attacks.
exclusions: An isolated octave does not form a supported octave passage.

methods.title: Separate Finger Lines
instructions: Practice the outer-finger line first, using finger 5 on white keys and finger 4 on black keys.
Then practice the finger-1 line with the same pitches in source order.

requirements: Write exactly two measures using eighth notes.
Use finger 5 on white keys, finger 4 on black keys, and finger 1 for the other octave pitch.
Use only the affected hand, or align both affected hands when both contain octaves.

methods.title: Dotted-Rhythm Variations
instructions: Practice the octaves first with a dotted-eighth and sixteenth rhythm.
Then reverse the pattern to sixteenth and dotted-eighth.

requirements: Write exactly two measures and retain both pitches of every octave.
Apply the transformation to the affected hand or hands.

methods.title: Expanding Five-Note Pattern
instructions: Play each pattern as fast and correctly as possible to build endurance.
Begin with two notes and add one scale note at a time until the pattern reaches five notes.

requirements: Start at the lowest source octave position and follow the original key signature.
Use eighth-note full octaves and generate each affected hand separately.

methods.title: Alternating Accent Octaves
instructions: Play each pattern as fast and correctly as possible to build endurance.
Accent the lowest and highest notes on the first and third beats.

requirements: Write two identical measures of eight eighth-note octaves using scale degrees 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2.
Follow the original key signature and expand to five notes even when the source is shorter.
Generate each affected hand separately and accent event indexes zero and four in each measure.

methods.title: Progressive Octave Groups
instructions: Add one octave at a time and rest after each group.
Continue the pattern yourself after the final printed continuation mark.

requirements: Use eighth-note full octaves and place a rest after every group.
Generate min(3, totalOctaveAttacks - 1) groups by adding one source octave per group.
Stop after the generated groups and print Etc. after the final group.

methods.title: Repeated Octave Accent Pairs
instructions: Repeat each octave twice, keeping the original passage order.
Accent the first note of each pair, then accent the second note in the next measure.

requirements: Write exactly two measures of eight eighth-note full octaves.
Use the first four source positions, or cycle shorter passages in their original order.
Accent event indexes zero, two, four, and six in measure one and one, three, five, and seven in measure two.
Generate each affected hand separately.

guardrails: Return exactly two different eligible exercises selected by the application-owned random variety policy.
Render the exercises on separate systems and never combine them into one exercise.
Follow the original key signature and use eighth notes except for the dotted-rhythm method.
Use finger 5 on white-key octaves, finger 4 on black-key octaves, and finger 1 for the other octave pitch.

techniques.title: Chord Jumps
detectionEvidence: Two or more distinct multi-note chord attacks with significant hand-position travel.
exclusions: Do not classify a single-note leap as a chord jump.

methods.title: Upper-Note Targets
instructions: Play only the highest source note of each chord and land gently at every destination.
Release between targets, then restore each complete chord without holding a stretch.

requirements: Keep the source register.
Add a short movement rest after each target.

methods.title: Lower-Group Targets
instructions: Play the remaining lower notes of each source chord together after removing only its top note.
Prepare each shape during the pause, then restore the whole chord sequence softly.

requirements: Keep lower tones simultaneous.
A two-note chord leaves one lower tone.

guardrails: The left-hand upper pitch is not automatically finger five.

techniques.title: Scales and Chromatic Runs
detectionEvidence: A rapid melodic line of mostly adjacent pitches with source accidentals retained.
exclusions: Exclude trill patterns and simultaneous double-note passages.

methods.title: Short Scale Groups
instructions: Practice three or four consecutive source notes slowly and release after each small group.
Join neighboring groups when even, then restore the entire run in its original rhythm.

requirements: Retain every pitch and accidental.
Write a rest after each group.

methods.title: Scale Rhythm Variants
instructions: Alternate long-short and short-long pairs while keeping every scale pitch clear and relaxed.
Use slow even notes for an irregular run, then restore all original durations.

requirements: Never guess thumb-crossing fingerings.
Do not force dotted rhythm onto an irregular line.

guardrails: Preserve supplied source fingering and never invent new fingering.

techniques.title: Arpeggios and Broken Chords
detectionEvidence: Successive chord tones in one hand across a register or hand-position change.
exclusions: Do not block a cell whose span is physically unsafe.

methods.title: Blocked Arpeggio Cells
instructions: Play each comfortable broken-chord cell once as a soft blocked chord and release.
Then play its source notes in order and restore the original arpeggio movement.

requirements: Add an explicit rest after each chord.
Use outer notes instead when the span is unsafe.

methods.title: Reduced Landing Study
instructions: Practice only the departure and arrival tones of each source arpeggio cell with travel time.
Restore the omitted inner tones after every landing is accurate and relaxed.

requirements: Keep real registers.
Replace omitted middle-note time with rests.

guardrails: Generated blocked chords are practice versions and do not alter original arpeggiation markings.

techniques.title: Large Single-Note Leaps
detectionEvidence: A hand travels between far-apart single notes whose endpoints are not simultaneous chords.
exclusions: Exclude chord jumps and successive chord-tone arpeggios.

methods.title: Departure and Arrival Pairs
instructions: Play each exact departure note, release, move lightly, pause over the target, and land.
Add the surrounding material only after the source landing is consistently accurate.

requirements: Keep pitch spelling and register.
Add a short rest after each arrival.

methods.title: Arrival Targets
instructions: Practice only the verified landing notes with enough silence to locate every position.
Then restore the departure notes, inner material, and original rhythm without stretching.

requirements: Space targets with rests.
Never transpose or invent a target.

guardrails: Keep travel light and do not maintain a stretched position between keys.

techniques.title: Repeated Notes and Chords
detectionEvidence: The same pitch or simultaneous chord is reattacked several times without ties.
exclusions: Changing chord locations are chord jumps, and tied sustains are not repetitions.

methods.title: Release and Reset
instructions: Play each repeated source note or chord clearly and release after every attack.
Let the wrist reset freely, then restore the original tempo without rigidity.

requirements: Preserve chord membership.
Use quarter or eighth attacks with rests.

methods.title: Grouped Repetitions
instructions: Practice every intended reattack in groups of two or three with a rest after each group.
Reconnect the groups while keeping the timing even and the wrist free.

requirements: Preserve every reattack.
Do not tie separate strikes.

guardrails: Do not diagnose an instrument-action problem as a technical fault.

techniques.title: Double Notes
detectionEvidence: Two non-octave simultaneous note lines move independently in one hand across consecutive attacks.
exclusions: Exclude octaves and stationary repeated chords.

methods.title: Separate Double-Note Lines
instructions: Practice the real upper line once and the real lower line once with even phrasing.
Then restore both lines together while preserving written legato, holds, and ties.

requirements: Label both miniature studies.
Use pitches from the real voices.

methods.title: Slow Double-Note Groups
instructions: Play the source pairs slowly in groups of two or three and release where permitted.
Restore the original articulation and sustained notes once the pairs align.

requirements: Keep each pair simultaneous.
Retain true tied or sustained notes.

guardrails: Do not flatten two independent source lines into invented pitches.

techniques.title: Trills and Ornaments
detectionEvidence: An explicit ornament with verified realization or a written rapid alternation with confirmed pitches.
exclusions: A symbol alone is insufficient when its auxiliary pitch or realization is unknown.

methods.title: Slow Ornament Alternation
instructions: Practice only the confirmed ornament pitches slowly and evenly with relaxed fingers.
Keep the verified accidentals, starting pitch, and final resolution when returning to context.

requirements: Use only verified written pitches and accidentals.

methods.title: Grouped Ornament Notes
instructions: Practice the confirmed ornament notes in groups of two to four with brief rests.
Connect the verified pattern only after each small group is clear and relaxed.

requirements: Never infer note count or realization from a symbol alone.

guardrails: Choose another supported technique or return a clear error rather than fabricate an ornament.

techniques.title: Hands Together and Polyrhythms
detectionEvidence: Two staves contain interlocking attacks or explicit source ratios such as two against three.
exclusions: Ordinary homorhythmic two-staff texture is not a polyrhythm.

methods.title: Hands Separately
instructions: Practice each source hand alone while preserving its genuine durations and tuplet groupings.
Count the shared beat slowly, then combine both hands without changing the ratio.

requirements: Label both hand-only passes.
Preserve explicit tuplets.

methods.title: Timing Skeleton
instructions: Play only the important aligned source attacks while keeping each hand's ratio intact.
Reinsert omitted notes after the structural timing feels secure and even.

requirements: Use rests for omissions.
Keep tuplets and aligned onsets rhythmically valid.

guardrails: Never flatten a source triplet into ordinary even subdivisions.

techniques.title: Melody over Accompaniment
detectionEvidence: An identifiable melodic voice and a separate supporting voice or staff.
exclusions: Do not assume that the highest pitch is automatically the melody.

methods.title: Melody Alone
instructions: Play the actual melodic voice alone with its source phrasing, durations, and dynamics.
Listen for an even singing line before restoring any accompaniment.

requirements: Maintain melody ties, rests, and articulations.

methods.title: Melody and Harmonic Skeleton
instructions: Add only the source bass or harmony changes needed to hear the structure beneath the melody.
Return to the complete accompaniment after the balance is comfortable and controlled.

requirements: Use valid rests for omitted support voices.
Retain the actual melody voice.

guardrails: Select melodic and harmonic voices from score evidence rather than register alone.

methods.title: Focused Reduction
instructions: Isolate the most consequential supported challenge using only the selected measure's musical material.
Practice the reduction slowly, then return to the complete source measure.

requirements: Keep the exercise piano-realistic and readable.

methods.title: Contrasting Variation
instructions: Use a distinct second transformation that addresses another supported feature of the measure.
Practice it slowly and restore the original rhythm, articulation, and musical intent.

requirements: Do not duplicate the first exercise.
